minutes.headline: Sewer Commission walked through the FY24 operating budget line by line; it shows a deficit and no rate decision was made.
minutes.summary: A special budget workshop where the Sewer Commission reviewed the preliminary FY24 operating budget with the departing staff member. Revenue, payroll, purchase of service, utilities, capital, debt and town meeting transfers were covered. Members raised pump station safety and manhole inspection concerns and agreed to a new consulting line, but left rate and retained-earnings choices for later meetings.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission sent its preliminary FY24 operating budget to the town manager as is, showing a deficit. It deferred the rate increase and retained-earnings use.
Members kept a new administrative consulting line in the preliminary budget.
The DPW director will review the 2020 pump station safety findings with the contractor and report back on whether the budget needs more.
Members held off on a separate safety line until that conversation, and left the OPEB line at a placeholder pending word from the accountant.
A resident who installed a deduct meter objected to the plumbing permit and sign-off requirement. The procedure goes on the next agenda.

why_it_matters: Sewer rates are what customers pay, and the draft budget has the rate increase at zero while still showing a deficit. Closing that gap will take a rate increase, a draw on retained earnings, or cuts, and the commission has not chosen among them.
Pump station safety and manhole inspection costs could add to the budget once the DPW director reports back, so the final figures may differ from this draft.
